problem: Augmenting QA models with external knowledge (knowledge graphs) either fails to model multi-hop relations efficiently or lacks transparency into the model's prediction rationale.
method: Multi-hop graph relation network (MHGRN): a knowledge-aware module added to a pretrained language model that performs multi-hop, multi-relational reasoning over external-KG subgraphs, unifying path-based methods with graph neural networks.
key_assumptions: Subgraphs extracted from an external knowledge graph can be encoded by a module bolted onto a pretrained language model
Unifying path-based reasoning and GNNs improves interpretability without losing scalability
main_contribution: MHGRN, a multi-hop graph relation network that equips pretrained language models with a module performing multi-hop, multi-relational reasoning over subgraphs extracted from external knowledge graphs, unifying path-based reasoning and GNNs for better interpretability and scalability.
results: Abstract: empirically shown effective and scalable on CommonsenseQA and OpenbookQA, with case studies interpreting behaviour.
limitations: Knowledge-aware QA over concept graphs (CommonsenseQA, OpenbookQA), not passage-grounded triple supervision for multi-hop QA.
The subgraph is used as model input, not as an enriched training target.
Does not study whether the provenance (same passage) of context triples matters.
code_availability: Code released for experiments according to the abstract ("with the code for experiments released"); exact URL not stated in abstract.

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: MHGRN is the canonical 'use the subgraph as model input' approach (GraftNet-family pre-processing is also used by the KBQA teacher-student line). The idea instead varies what supervision the LM sees (isolated triple vs passage-coherent group) and asks whether context is the active ingredient — a question MHGRN does not pose because it never trains on isolated triples as a control.
relation_to_idea.basis: Problem overlap 0.5: both are multi-hop reasoning over KG subgraphs for QA, and both use a subgraph rather than isolated triples. Method overlap 0.3: MHGRN adds a reasoning module over a subgraph at model level; the idea adds context triples as supervision text and compares two training regimes. Evaluation overlap 0.25: CommonsenseQA/OpenbookQA multiple-choice differs from multi-hop KBQA with hop-depth transfer.
